subject: DIAGNOSED s322: `-f _` (perl's stat-cache filehandle) is emitted as a bare variable → unbound-variable crash
description:
FULLY DIAGNOSED s322, NOT fixed (session ended; the half-written runtime edit was reverted so the tree is clean).

SYMPTOM: 12 of the 61 FAIL files in the widened CPAN board (Data-Dump 10, Algorithm-Diff 2) die with "The variable Test::_ is unbound". 3-line repro:
    use Test;  BEGIN { plan tests => 1 }  ok(1);

ROOT CAUSE — nothing to do with $_ or with packages. Test.pm line 200 is
    ... and -e $file and -f _ and -r _;
`_` there is perl's STAT-CACHE FILEHANDLE ("reuse the buffer from the last stat, do not stat again") — an everyday idiom for avoiding three stat(2) calls. PCL emits it as a bare CL symbol: (p--f _). That symbol has no binding, so it is an unbound-variable crash in whatever package the code happens to live in. Confirmed by handler: SYMBOL-NAME="_" PACKAGE="Test" — note the missing `$`; it is not a variable at all.

Same family as CLAUDE.md rule 12: an unimplemented case surfacing as an internal CL error instead of a Perl-level one.

DESIGNED FIX (runtime only, ~30 lines, no parser change — every emission path that produces the bareword `_` is then handled at once, per CLAUDE.md 11):
 1. `(defvar _ '%pcl-stat-cache)` in :pcl + `#:_` in the export list, so any generated package that (:use :pcl) resolves the same symbol. Safe: Perl subs are emitted as `pl-*`, Perl scalars keep their `$`, so nothing else claims the bare `_`.
 2. `(defvar *pcl-stat-cache-path* nil)` + `(defun %p--path (file) ...)`: a real operand is remembered, the marker reads the remembered one, `_` before any stat yields "" (every test then reports false).
 3. Replace `(to-string (unbox file))` with `(%p--path file)` in the filetest family — p--e p--d p--f p--r p--w p--x p--s p--z, plus the three shared helpers %p--stat-test, %p--file-age, %p--text-scan. (%p--stat-test/-file-age/-text-scan already exist, so this is a small, mechanical edit set.)
 4. `%p-stat-arg` (stat/lstat) must both FEED the cache and honour `_`, so `stat $f; -f _` works.
 DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE to document in the docstring: perl caches the stat BUFFER and does not re-stat; PCL caches the PATH and stats again. Same answer except in a race, and it keeps each test's own logic (access(2) for -r/-w/-x, lstat for -l) instead of reimplementing perl's buffer-vs-syscall table.

TEST when fixed: a Pl/t row for `-e $f and -f _ and -r _`, `stat $f; -f _`, and `-f _` with no preceding stat; then re-run the two dists (Data-Dump, Algorithm-Diff) through tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl and diff docs/cpan-scoreboard.tsv.

ALSO NOTED while in there: transpiling perl's Test.pm standalone prints "Handle single node of unknown type: ref=''" — a separate codegen gap worth a look.
